Variants.Content: Wild orcs are the most primitive branch of the greenskins - they reject any metal weapons and armor, and are naked only covered with magical war patterns, but they rampage on the battlefield with pure feral fury. These primitive warriors from the most barbaric corners of the mainland believed that iron tools would cut off the soul connection with Brother Goge Mao.

The wild boys are really crazy! You know that other greenskins - including me - love heavy armor and machetes, right? But the wild orcs think iron is dirty! They said that the blue and white war patterns on their bodies were more effective at blocking swords and guns than iron armor. I used to think it was a fart - but then I saw with my own eyes a barbarian boss who was hit in the chest by three crossbow arrows. The tools they used were all ripped from the bones of giant beasts - big tooth clubs, bone knives, and monitor lizard skulls used as shields - those bones were more powerful than my iron ax in the hands of the wild orcs! But the wild boys are too straight-minded. When fighting, they only know how to rush forward, unlike us who sneak around behind and hit the black stick. But if you put a group of wild boys at the front of Waaagh as the vanguard of the charge - then they will be worth all their teeth, because nothing can stop a crazy wild orc!

Savage Orcs are a double-edged sword in tactical evaluation. Its core advantage is the unparalleled impact during the charge phase - the magic war pattern will indeed activate some kind of primitive protective field when the fighting spirit is high, making the survival rate of the Savage Orcs in the first two charge contacts about three times higher than that of all light infantry units. But their disadvantage is equally fatal: once the charge fails to break the enemy's line, the lack of armor of the wild orcs has almost zero resistance to sustained fighting-especially the spear phalanx and concentrated shooting of crossbow bolts. There are three tactical points: first, the decisive moment and direction of the Savage Orcs entering the battle must be accurately determined to the foot level; second, their flanks must be protected by heavily armored units; third, before the Savage Orcs charge, a large number of long-range shots must be used to weaken the enemy's morale - the Savage Orcs' biggest weapon is not their bone clubs, but the fear generated by the opponent when they see a group of naked giant beasts covered with ghostly war patterns rushing towards them screaming.

The technical taboo of the wild orcs - the rejection of all metals - does not originate from any doctrinal text (the green skin has no writing), but an ancient ecological adaptation passed on through bloodline memory. Within the framework of greenskin spore ecology, the spore lineage of the Savage Orcs is considered to be the oldest of all greenskin subspecies, and its genetic memory retains the original fighting form code that predates the "Iron Age Greenskins". When they come into contact with metal, the symbiotic colonies on the body surface - the biological truth of the so-called "magic war marks" - will produce an electrochemical stress reaction, causing the individual orcs to experience severe discomfort and a spike in aggression - this is the root of the biological instinct of the wild orcs to regard iron as "dirty" and tend to destroy it, rather than abstract beliefs. The protective effect of its war pattern has been preliminarily confirmed by the Imperial Academy of Magic: the luminous substance in the war pattern pigment is a rare fluorescent fungal extract, which will generate a trace amount of ether force field after being activated by orc adrenaline. The intensity of its protective effect is linearly related to the fighting spirit (physiological excitement) of the wild orcs. This is why a calm wild orc can be shot by ordinary arrows, but a furious wild orc has almost iron armor defense in a short period of time.

I have always had a morbid curiosity about the war marks of wild orcs. I read a record brought back by an imperial explorer in the southern wilderness: He said that the war patterns of the wild orcs were not painted on - they were created by tribal wizards who injected the "essence" of Gormao Er Ge - a glowing green mucus - directly into the orcs' blood vessels, and then the paint spread along the blood vessels to the body surface. This means that under each war pattern is a vein, and the war pattern is actually a map of living meridians. This belief in both worshiping and destroying one’s own body fascinates and terrifies me.

When my family was fighting a defensive war in the south, we encountered a tribe of barbaric orcs - they had migrated from the southern wilderness and did not know any civilization at all. After our defenders shot down a wild orc, they discovered that his bone knife was engraved with the pattern of my family's emblem - it was the bone knife of a giant lizard belonging to the captain of a dwarf expedition that never came back after going on an expedition seventy years ago. The fact that a wild orc was wielding a relic from my great-grandfather's time as a weapon kept me awake for several nights.

In the southern wilderness, I came across an altar of wild orcs - a mountain of huge beast skulls, estimated to be twenty or thirty feet high, and each skull was painted with blue and white war patterns. What I remember most clearly is the smell: not rancid, but the smell of spicy burning plant smoke, mixed with fresh earthy smell. We only stayed there for less than a quarter of an hour before we withdrew, because we heard the sound of drums in the distance - the drums of wild orcs, which were extremely low and deep, like something huge moving under the ground. The kind of drum beat that makes your heart beat so fast we had to cover our ears and run.

I am an iron ore merchant in the territory of the Border Prince. The biggest enemy of my business is not my competitors, but the wild orcs. They didn't know the ore was valuable - they simply hated iron. The tribes of wild orcs will constantly attack our transport convoys. Instead of grabbing the iron, they will throw the iron into the swamp or bury it. Other orcs steal iron to make armor, while wild orcs steal iron to destroy iron. This nearly tripled our transportation costs, as each convoy had to hire at least two teams of mercenaries to escort it.
